text.p: Forstmann & Co Inc said on Thursday it had emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy and entered into a new credit facility.
The company, which filed for protection under Chapter 11 of U.S. bankruptcy law in September 1995, said it finished the transactions provided for under its reorganization plan.
Forstmann said it also entered a credit facility provided by a syndicate of financial institutions led by BankAmerica Business Credit Inc.
The three year facility consisted of a $31.45 million term loan and a revolving credit facility under which Forstmann could borrow up to $85 million, it said.
The facility would be used to refinance most of Forstmann's existing secured debt and to fund distributions under the reorganization plan, the company said.

"Our balance sheet is stonger and the financing terms are more favorable to us," said Rod Peckham, Forstmann chief financial officer. "In addition, our long term debt today is nearly half what it was when the restructuring process began."
Holders of general unsecured claims against Forstmann would be issued 50 shares of the new common stock for each $1,000 of allowed general unsecured claims, it said.
Forstmann also said it was seeking to list its new common stock on Nasdaq.
